---
title: "Reader"
subtitle: "Read the papers in your library, with annotations that stick"
---

Reader is where you actually read. Open a paper from the [Library](library.qmd) (the **Read**
action on a row, or **Ctrl+Shift+click**) and you get a fast PDF view whose highlights and
notes anchor to the *text itself* — they survive re-downloads, re-opens, and zooming, and they
belong to the paper, not to any one project.

# Getting around

The toolbar carries the essentials: zoom (**+** / **−**, **0** fits the width, **⤢** fits the
page height; **Ctrl+scroll** or a pinch zooms at the cursor), a page-layout picker (**1-up**,
**2-up**, **Grid**, **Row**), and a page-number box to jump anywhere. **PageUp/PageDown** and
**Home/End** work as you'd expect, and after you follow a link or outline entry, the **←**
button in the toolbar takes you back to where you were.

The panel icons at each end of the toolbar show and hide the sidebars — **Ctrl+B** for the
left one, **Ctrl+Shift+B** for the right.

Two sidebars flank the page, and both are **drag-resizable** — pull the edge beside either
one, or double-click it to go back to the default width. The left sidebar has four tabs:

- **References** — the paper's own reference list (once the paper is
  [enriched](library.qmd#enrich)): each entry expands to its abstract, can be added to your
  library with **+ FluxLib**, or opened by DOI. When an entry is already in your library
  *and* its PDF is on disk, the row offers **Open PDF** — one click and it's a new tab.
- **Cited by** — the papers that cite *this* one, looked up from OpenAlex. Sort by **Most
  cited** (influential follow-ups first) or **Newest**, and hit **⟳** to re-query. The list
  is cached, so coming back to it is instant and works offline; rows behave exactly like
  reference rows, Open PDF included. (Needs the paper enriched, for its OpenAlex id.)
- **Search** — find-in-document, below.
- **Outline** — the PDF's bookmarks, click to jump.

Each paper remembers its own page, zoom, and layout between sessions; the sidebar widths are
a workspace setting shared by every paper.

# Searching your library while you read

**Alt+R** — the same chord as the manuscript writer's reference search — opens a **Library**
panel in the right sidebar, next to your annotations. Search the whole reference library by
title, author, year, journal, or citekey (`author:siclari year:2017` works, as in the
Library), and open any hit's **PDF** as a tab or its **DOI** in your browser. Papers already
open as tabs are marked. The panel is a panel, not a popup: it stays until you switch back to
the **Annotations** tab, so you can keep it beside you while you read.

# Tabs

Every paper you open becomes a **tab** in the strip above the toolbar, so a few papers stay a
click apart — no re-finding them in the Library. Opening an already-open paper just focuses
its tab. Switching between recently viewed tabs is instant, with your page, zoom, and even a
search in progress exactly as you left them; tabs you haven't looked at in a while reload on
demand, restored to their remembered page and zoom.

- **Ctrl+Tab** / **Ctrl+Shift+Tab** (or **Ctrl+PageDown** / **Ctrl+PageUp**) cycle through tabs.
- **Ctrl+W**, a **middle-click**, or the tab's **×** closes one — the next tab over takes its place.
- **Drag a tab** along the strip to reorder it.
- Your open tabs (and which was active) come back when you restart Flux.

## Two papers side by side

**Alt-click** (or **Cmd-click**) a tab to open that paper in a second pane beside the current
one — compare a method against the paper that introduced it, or keep a review open while you
read. Each pane has its own tab strip and switches independently; tab shortcuts act on the
pane you're focused in. You can even show the *same* paper in both panes — a highlight made
in one appears in the other. (Alt-clicking the Reader icon in the top bar splits too, as in
every mode.)

# Highlights and notes

Select any text and a small color menu appears — five highlight colors (yellow, green, blue,
pink, orange). Click one and the highlight is saved. Click a highlight later to open its
popover: recolor it, attach a **comment**, copy the text, or delete it. The right sidebar's
**Annotations** tab (**Alt+A**) lists every annotation with its page; click one to scroll to
it, and edit or delete from there.

Annotations are anchored by the quoted text (with a little context on each side), not by pixel
positions — so they re-attach correctly even if the PDF is re-fetched. If a paper's text
changes so much that a quote can't be found, the note is kept and marked *detached* rather
than lost.

**Export notes…** (on the Annotations tab, and on the paper's row in the Library) writes all of a
paper's highlights and comments to a tidy Markdown file — grouped by page, quotes with your
notes beneath, citation and DOI in the header — ready to drop into your own notes system.

# Search

**Ctrl+F** opens the **Search** tab in the left sidebar. Every match in the document is
listed there with the text around it, grouped by the section it falls in (or by page, for
PDFs without a bookmark outline) — so you can see all your hits at once instead of stepping
blindly through them. Click any result to jump straight to it, or work through them in order
with **‹ ›** (or **Enter** / **Shift+Enter** in the query box). Matches stay highlighted
throughout the document, with the current one picked out. **Escape** clears the query and
leaves the pane open. (Arriving from a full-text `ft:` search in the Library lands you here
with the search already run.)

# Figures and snips

- **Alt+drag** a region of the page to **pop out a figure**: the region floats in its own
  panel beside the text — study a figure and the paragraph discussing it side by side, drag it
  around, resize it, jump back to its page.
- **Ctrl+Alt+drag** a region to capture a **paper snip**: a high-resolution PNG saved into
  your current project's `plots/paper_snips/`, after a quick naming popover. The snip carries
  its provenance — paper, page, and formatted citation — *inside the file*, so when you later
  place it in a [figure](figure.qmd) or slide, "copy citation" still knows where it came from.
  (Snips need a project open, since they save into it.)

# Citation peek

Hover any citation link in the PDF and a card shows what it cites — authors, year, title, and
how often it's been cited — with one-click **+ FluxLib** to grab it, or a jump to the
bibliography entry. Follow it, and **←** brings you back.

# Supplements

The **⧉ PDF** switcher in the toolbar flips between the main paper and its supplementary
files, and **Add supplement…** attaches new ones. Supplements live beside the paper in your
library; highlights always anchor to the main text.

# The terminal

**Alt+T** opens a terminal drawer under the paper — run `flux principal` (or `claude`,
`codex`, whatever you use) there and you have
[your collaborator](../agents/collaboration.qmd) beside the paper. Drag the drawer's top edge
to resize it; double-click that edge to reset it.

Select any text and press the **✦** button that appears — or the one on a highlight's
popover — to **send that passage to the terminal**. It is typed in for you, never sent, so
you can add your own question before pressing Enter. Whatever agent is running there can also
read your live reading context — which paper, which page, your highlights — so "what does this
figure mean?" needs no copy-pasting.

# Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause → fix |
|---|---|
| "No PDF on disk" when opening | The paper's PDF isn't fetched yet → **Get PDF** in the Library |
| Reference list is empty | The paper isn't enriched → **Enrich** in the Library |
| A highlight shows as *detached* | The stored quote no longer matches this PDF's text — the note is preserved; re-highlight to re-anchor it |
| Snip capture says "Open a project" | Snips save into the current project's `plots/` — open one first |
